description: The Organizational Technical Alpha program structure: waves, lanes, and the bounded slices under them, each routed to the issue/PR/truth-owner that actually owns it. This file owns SEQUENCING AND STATUS ROUTING ONLY. It never restates a domain fact another owner holds: where a wave depends on identity semantics, it names docs/architecture/IDENTITY_SEMANTICS.md rather than summarising it. A cold-start agent should be able to reconstruct the programme from here plus the routers it names, with no chat history.
reconciliation_note: Every entry carries a status drawn from a closed set. STILL_VALID / REFINED / SUPERSEDED / BLOCKED_ON_HUMAN_DECISION / DEFERRED_NOT_ABANDONED / OBSOLETE. A wave that has not started is not 'in progress', and a design that has been reviewed is not implemented. Reconciled against live repository evidence 2026-09-01; where evidence changed the trajectory the change is recorded in the entry rather than silently applied.

target.statement: One reproducibly deployed and recoverable two-node ICN environment, running one current identity/authority generation, producing independently verifiable evidence, with one complete institutional workflow exercised end to end by humans -- including a governance action and a bounded resource action -- and every unproven capability an explicit non-claim.
target.not_completion: Technical Alpha completion is NOT green CI, a test count, or a merged PR. Those are necessary conditions for trusting the evidence, never the evidence itself.

generation_convergence.statement: Technical Alpha is primarily a GENERATION-CONVERGENCE event, not an attempt to invent every subsystem. ICN already contains strong proof islands built across different architectural generations; the goal is to select one exact current identity/authority profile and make identity, authority, governance, resource execution, receipts, evidence, recovery, node deployment and human workflow describe the same system at the same semantic generation.

generations.A: Practical integrated system. DID stood in for person/member/device/node in many runtime paths, but governance, execution, receipts and the organiser loop worked well enough for integrated proofs.
generations.B: Architectural decomposition specified: Principal != Human Subject != Institution != Node; account/resource != identity; authentication != authority != standing.
generations.C: Partially implemented current substrate: N1 authority log, canonical N2 semantics, I7 Principal equality, stronger SessionAuthority, networking/authentication hardening.
generations.missing_proof: Generation C driving the Generation A institutional/economic vertical. That is the convergence problem the Alpha exists to close.

rules: Do not infer semantics that another layer owns. YAML syntax -> a YAML parser. Shell evaluation -> the shell, or a repository-owned executable. Principal identity -> the identity layer. Subject authority -> the authority layer. Institutional recognition -> GEN/governance. Program state -> the actual truth owners, routed by icn#2689.
When a validator grows an endless series of exceptions, the abstraction boundary is wrong. Investigate that before the fifth syntax-specific patch, not the tenth.
A dependency change is not one edit. It is every execution surface that runs the thing, and every authoritative or generated description of that surface.
Write the supported input domain down. An unwritten domain cannot terminate a review, because no counterexample can be classified as out of scope.
A green gate is not proof the mechanism proves its claim. Ask whether the test passed for the right reason, and mutation-test the control against the code it was written to catch.

structure: Program -> Wave -> Lane -> Bounded Slice -> Checkpoint. A slice is bounded when it has one owning issue, one reviewable change, and evidence that can be reproduced without this file.

router.role: Program router and restart checkpoint. It sequences and points; it does not hold domain facts. Follow: #2689 -> current wave -> lane -> bounded issue/spec -> implementation PR -> architecture truth owner -> required evidence -> next checkpoint.

vertical_institution.note: The complete institutional proof target. Wave 4 exercises it end to end; Wave 5 puts real organisers through it and captures where the HUMAN system fails. No claim of live federation, payment network, production adoption or banking semantics is implied.

development_factory.note: Wave 0 is an on-ramp, not the project.

0.name: Control-plane reconciliation
0.note: Nearly closed. Its lasting output is not the validators but the doctrine in framing.engineering_doctrine and two written input-domain contracts.

slices.note: Provider-aware agent registry. Closure rule adopted icn#2689: a finding blocks freeze only if it falsifies a claimed behaviour, mis-accepts or mis-rejects an in-contract configuration, breaks a required execution surface, or makes stated semantics materially false.
Prompt-content truth ownership: stale reachable agent doctrine, especially superseded identity semantics. Split separable semantic classes into bounded issues rather than one mega-change.
Hook execution semantics. The checker owns a deliberately tiny invocation language and does not own Bash.

1.name: Exact Technical Alpha core candidate / semantic generation convergence
1.note: Selects one exact revision/profile and one identity/authority generation. Blocked on Wave 0 closing, then driven by the semantic vertical below.

3.name: Ecosystem semantic reconciliation
3.note: Downstream repos aligned to the same ICN semantic generation. No downstream repo currently holds a human-signed ICN lock; agents may prepare, only humans sign.

5.name: Actual organizer rehearsal
5.note: Real organisers through the workflow, capturing where the human system fails. Not a synthetic API demo.

semantic_alpha_vertical.note: One falsifiable vertical: current-generation human governance front end driving the EXISTING resource/economic tail. Do not invent a replacement economic engine to make the vertical aesthetically uniform -- the existing allocation/settlement/execution/journal machinery is sound and its proof is reused.

order.what: Durable local AuthorityFactStore plus restart rehydration. Identity owns the fact interface; the runtime owns the persistent adapter. Proves local durable custody only, NOT N3 replication, and governance must not become the owner of human identity facts merely because it consumes them.
Immutable SubjectRecognitionV1. Recognition is not ownership: an institution recognising a Subject does not create or own it.

LegacyPrincipalV1 vs ContextSubjectV1, with an empty legacy membership list for the Alpha domain as defence in depth. Old DID-vote endpoints reject ContextSubjectV1 domains. Do not migrate all existing domains.

Relying-party-selected historical authorisation evaluation. Later ordinary revocation must prevent future acts, not rewrite a previously valid act as unauthored; fork/superseding evidence over the relevant prefix fails closed rather than choosing a branch.
Bounded canonical proposal/effect commitment plus a frozen VotingProcessSnapshotV1. Alpha uses Majority + explicit closure; wall-clock deadlines are deliberately NOT part of the security proof.

Authenticated Principal + acting Subject + institutional context, with a narrow governance:subject-vote capability. A session answers 'may this request enter this handler now'; it is not historical authorship.
Preview of exact bytes, canonical MemberVoteActionV1, local device signature, immutable one-ballot storage. V1 scope is ONE human action: Vote.
Process-bound decision hash. Justified because V3 binds no proposal/effect payload -- verified in crates/icn-governance/src/proof.rs.
The V4 decision hash into the EXISTING allocation, settlement intent, execution and journal. Do not teach allocation/settlement/ledger code what a SubjectId is; that semantic firewall is a feature.
Offline verification with the producer stopped, tamper-negative evidence, encrypted destroy/restore continuity.

semantic_alpha_vertical.ballot_identity: The durable ballot slot is keyed by (process_hash, SubjectId), NOT by device Principal. One Subject with two authorised devices is two signers and one institutional voter.

gen_a_invariants.derivation: GovernanceDomainV1 context + public context_salt[32] + GEN domain/version framing -> SHA-256 -> the EXISTING opaque N1 ContextNonce[32] -> unchanged N1 inception -> SubjectId. Verified against crates/icn-identity/src/authority_log/body.rs: ContextNonce is [u8; 32] with a public const from_bytes, so GEN needs no N1 wire change.
gen_a_invariants.determinism_correction: Do NOT claim 'same secret + same salt = same Subject'. N1 inception commits next_commitment, which depends on the retained continuity plan/horizon -- verified in authority_log/construct.rs, where commitment() folds kind_at(g) and authority_set(g) from horizon() down. Deterministic re-derivation requires the retained continuity secret AND establishment plan/horizon AND GEN context descriptor AND context_salt.
gen_a_invariants.reference_split: subject_context_ref_hash (context/salt + inception EventId) is the stable recognition basis. initial_device_binding_ref_hash (context reference + initial authorize EventId) is separate. Institutional recognition must never be permanently coupled to the first device.
gen_a_invariants.bootstrap_capabilities: The initial N1 device authorisation grants Sign and Present only. No Recover, no shared root key, no global registrar, no global public Person ID. N7 owns generalised recovery.

semantic_distinctions.note: Do not let future mapping collapse these. Each names a different thing that a single DID used to stand in for.

terms.Subject: Context-bound human/member identity.
terms.Device Principal: A cryptographic actor authorised to act for a Subject.
terms.Institution / governance domain: A governed collective context. NOT reducible to a custodian key.
terms.Authority facts: Evidence of who may act for a Subject.
terms.Recognition: Institutional acknowledgement of a Subject. Not creation, not ownership.
terms.Authorization: Historical authority evaluated at a point or process.
terms.Member-origin action: A device-authored action attributable through Subject semantics.
terms.Governance process: Proposal, frozen rules, eligible set, participation, deterministic close.

prohibitions: Do not reduce an institution to a custodian key.
Do not turn SubjectId into a global Person identifier.
Do not make the first device part of stable Subject recognition identity.
Do not let current-generation commitments use an arbitrary DID spelling where the intended concept is Principal identity (see icn#2627).
